label: Chemicals
summary: Cleaners, pool chemicals, solvents, pesticides, oils and industrial residues can burn skin and eyes, poison you when breathed or swallowed, or react dangerously when mixed. Old, leaking and unlabelled containers are the worst.
signs: Drums, jugs and tubs with warning symbols, or with no label at all
Sharp, sweet or choking smells, or stinging eyes when you walk in
Crystals or crust around caps and on shelves
Dead plants or stained ground around a storage area
Pool supply and farm supply stores, cleaning cupboards, workshops and labs
do: Read the label before you open anything
Open containers outdoors, or with doors and windows open
Keep chemicals in their original containers, closed and labelled
Store chlorine, acids, fuels and fertilisers well apart from each other
Leave at once if you start coughing or your eyes burn
Wash hands and face before eating
dont: Never mix chemicals: bleach with ammonia or with acid makes toxic gas
Don't sniff a container to find out what it is
Don't store chemicals in food or drink containers
Don't pour chemicals on the ground near wells, streams or gardens
Don't open bulging or rusted-through drums
Don't leave pet poisons about: ethylene-glycol antifreeze tastes sweet and a small amount can kill, and metaldehyde slug pellets cause tremors and seizures in dogs and cats within 1-4 hours.

Don't dose pets from the medicine box: acetaminophen is far more toxic to cats than to dogs, and ibuprofen can cause ulcers and kidney damage in dogs. Keep lilies, such as Easter lily, away from cats: they can cause kidney failure.
ppe: Gloves matched to the chemical on the maker’s chart. Thin nitrile is splash protection only: acetone, methanol and many solvents get through in about a minute, so change gloves at once after a splash
Indirect-vent goggles, with a face shield over them when pouring
Long sleeves and trousers, plus an apron and rubber boots for pouring
A respirator with the right cartridges if you have one. A dust mask does not stop vapour, cartridges run out without warning, and no filter mask works in a confined space or against carbon monoxide
firstAid: On skin: take off contaminated clothing, shoes and jewellery, brush off any powder, then rinse with plenty of clean water for at least 20 minutes

In an eye: rinse with clean running water for at least 15 minutes, holding the lids open and taking out contact lenses; keep rinsing longer for lye, drain cleaner, cement or lime, and get medical help
Breathed in: get to fresh air and rest; coughing, wheezing or chest tightness needs medical help, and breathing can get worse up to a day later, so keep watching them
Swallowed: rinse the mouth, don't make them vomit, keep the container to show a medic, and get medical help
Anyone drowsy, confused or struggling to breathe needs medical care urgently
Unresponsive but breathing: lay them on their side so they can't choke; not breathing normally: start CPR, with chest compressions only if there is chemical on their mouth
If any phone works, call a poison centre or emergency number and have the container or label in hand
